newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco cuts sentence on pharmacist over blood case.
newsitem.headline: Morocco cuts sentence on pharmacist over blood case.

text.p: A Moroccan court on Wednesday cut to six years a jail term imposed on a pharmacist charged with importing blood products contaminated with the HIV virus which causes AIDS, the Moroccan news agency MAP said.
Mohamed Benabderrazik, a Casablanca pharmacist, was sentenced to nine years imprisonment in April last year. The prosecution had asked for the maximum 10-year sentence.

During his trial, Benabderrazik pleaded innocent and his defence lawyers produced two leading haematologists who disputed the government's findings on the contaminated products. The pharmacist also argued that he did not intend to commercialise the samples.
The lower court last year acquitted two customs officers who had been charged with complicity in the affair.
